correctness.rationale: I reconstructed the deterministic map proof. The uniform forcing bound is 3T, so the strict subcritical recursion absorbs in any square of radius greater than 3T/(1−|1−T|). At T=2, subtracting X from F²(X) cancels the bias exactly. If |X_j| is at least R=11+arctanh(9/10)/α, both arguments in the j-th tanh difference have magnitude above arctanh(9/10), with opposite signs. The diagonal contribution gives inward signed movement even against the worst cross-coordinate contribution. My rational recheck gives inward margin 53/25 and displacement at most 54/5<R, excluding sign overshoot in this region. A coordinate outside R+54/5 decreases until it enters, and one inside stays inside, independently of the other coordinate. For the resulting F²-invariant absorbing square B, B∪F(B) gives F-absorption including odd iterates. For q=T−1>1, the increments of (−q)^(−n)X_n are bounded by 3T q^(−n−1); summing the geometric tail gives the claimed error and the lower bound on the amplitude, hence the exact growth rate outside the stated radius. At (T,α)=(9/4,1/4), H has global Lipschitz factor 27/40 and the fixed point has norm at most 12/13. On the unit square the tanh derivative with respect to the coordinate lies in [15/64,1/4]. My row-sum recheck gives diagonal extrema −181/512 and −47/160 and cross bound 9/16, hence 469/512. This puts the entire claimed 1/13 square in the contraction region; the escape radius at the same parameters is 27.
residual_risks: Exact real map only; neither finite precision nor stochastic dynamics is controlled. The escape radius is sufficient, not asserted optimal; absorption time depends on the start and on α.

value.rationale: At the neutral affine multiplier the standard textbook recursion is silent. A uniform two-step inward mechanism resolves exactly where all-start boundedness fails in a published model. The explicit coexisting attraction and escape regions distinguish what a locally stable equilibrium or a finite-initial-condition bifurcation plot can say from global stability.
